label: Postgres
summary: Connections, transactions, locks, cache hits, replication, checkpoints
source: postgres_exporter (prometheus-community), default collectors. Metric names checked against its documented default set; re-check on an exporter major version. Tools' names checked 2026-10-08 against Telegraf's inputs.postgresql (postgresql.go: it reads pg_stat_database and pg_stat_bgwriter only, so anything from pg_stat_activity, pg_settings or replication needs inputs.postgresql_extensible and has no name here), Datadog's postgres metadata.csv and util.py, the OpenTelemetry postgresqlreceiver documentation.md, and the AWS/RDS and Aurora CloudWatch metric lists, all at master/main. Datadog's activity metrics need collect_activity_metrics; OTel's deadlocks, temp and wal.delay metrics are off by default, and its wal.lag is not named: the receiver's postgresqlreceiver.preciselagmetrics gate (beta, so on, since v0.89.0) records wal.delay in its place (metadata.yaml and scraper.go, checked 2026-10-09); CloudWatch's Deadlocks and BufferCacheHitRatio exist on Aurora only. A ratio or a sum of a tool's metrics is null: export the computed series under the catalogue's name. The six KPIs added on 2026-10-09 were read that day at master. locks.waiting and transactions.idle.in.tx read pg_stat_activity_count's wait_event_type and state labels (the exporter's built-in queries before 0.20.0, its stat_activity collector from 0.20.0, under the same name and labels); the wait_event_type label needs postgres_exporter 0.17.0 or later (absent from v0.16.0's cmd/postgres_exporter, present at v0.17.0, checked 2026-10-09). An exporter writes no Lock row while nobody waits, so locks.waiting adds 'or 0 * max by (instance) (pg_up)' (checked on petstore's idle catalog-pg on 2026-10-27: one series per instance, labelled instance only, 0); on an older exporter, which writes no wait_event_type label at all, it therefore reads its 0 fallback whatever waits. checkpoints.requested reads stat_bgwriter's pg_stat_bgwriter_checkpoints_req_total up to PostgreSQL 16 and, from 17, which moved the count to pg_stat_checkpointer, pg_stat_checkpointer_num_requested_total, whose stat_checkpointer collector is off by default. The slot query reads pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn) per slot (the built-in queries before 0.20.0, the replication_slots collector from 0.20.0, under the same name). locks.waiting names no Datadog or OTel metric: Datadog's postgresql.locks covers only the relations listed under relations and postgresql.waiting_queries counts every wait event, not only locks, and OTel's postgresql.database.locks cannot tell a waiting lock from a held one. Telegraf's inputs.postgresql never reads pg_stat_checkpointer, so on PostgreSQL 17 it has no checkpoints_req; Datadog and OTel read it there (Datadog's util.py, OTel's client.go). CloudWatch's CommitThroughput is Aurora PostgreSQL only; OldestReplicationSlotLag is RDS and Aurora PostgreSQL.

metrics.name: up
metrics.label: Exporter can reach the database
metrics.description: 1 while postgres_exporter can connect to the database, 0 when it cannot. Any 0 during the run means the database was unreachable for at least one scrape. An exporter that goes with its target (a sidecar, a deleted pod) leaves no 0, only a gap: a short gap reads PASS, and one longer than the coverage floor allows reads LOW COVERAGE.

metrics.name: connections.used.pct
metrics.label: Connections used (%)
metrics.description: Backends connected, as a percentage of max_connections. Near 100 % new connections start to be refused.

metrics.name: connections.active
metrics.label: Active connections
metrics.description: Backends currently executing a query (state = active).

datadog.note: needs collect_activity_metrics; export the sum by host. Sessions of the postgres user are not counted

metrics.name: transaction.longest.seconds
metrics.label: Longest open transaction (s)
metrics.description: Age of the oldest transaction still open. A long one holds locks and blocks vacuum.

datadog.note: needs collect_activity_metrics; export the max by host

metrics.name: transactions.idle.in.tx
metrics.label: Sessions idle in transaction
metrics.description: Sessions that began a transaction and sit idle without ending it: a pool leak, or code that holds a transaction open across a remote call. Each keeps its locks and its connection slot.

datadog.note: needs collect_activity_metrics; export the sum by host

metrics.name: rollback.ratio.pct
metrics.label: Rolled-back transactions (%)
metrics.description: Rollbacks as a percentage of all finished transactions, per minute. A rise under load usually means conflicts or application errors.

metrics.name: throughput.commits
metrics.label: Commits per second (avg)
metrics.description: Transactions committed per second, averaged over the run. A floor shows the database received the load: it stays low when the traffic never reached it, because something upstream answered or the test pointed at another environment.

telegraf.note: one series per db tag: export the sum per server

datadog.note: one series per db tag: export the sum by host

otel.note: one series per database: export the sum per server

cloudwatch.note: Aurora PostgreSQL only; statistic Average, per DBInstanceIdentifier

metrics.name: locks.waiting
metrics.label: Sessions waiting on a lock
metrics.description: Sessions blocked on a lock another session holds, usually on a hot row or table. Brief waits are normal; a count that climbs with the load turns into timeouts. Reads 0 while nobody waits: postgres_exporter writes no Lock row then, so the query adds a 0 for each server pg_up reports.

metrics.name: deadlocks
metrics.label: Deadlocks per minute (peak)
metrics.description: Deadlocks detected in any minute of the run. Any is worth looking at.

telegraf.note: one series per db tag: export the sum per server

datadog.note: one series per db tag: export the sum by host

otel.note: off by default: enable it under the postgresql receiver's metrics; export the sum per server

cloudwatch.note: Aurora PostgreSQL only; statistic Average at a 1-minute period, per DBInstanceIdentifier

metrics.name: cache.hit.pct
metrics.label: Cache hit ratio (%)
metrics.description: Blocks served from shared buffers as a percentage of all blocks read, per minute. A drop under load means the working set no longer fits in memory.

cloudwatch.note: Aurora PostgreSQL only; statistic Minimum, per DBInstanceIdentifier

metrics.name: replication.lag.seconds
metrics.label: Replication lag (s)
metrics.description: How far a replica is behind its primary. A primary reports 0 (postgres_exporter), so match the replicas, or judge across: max.

otel.note: off by default: enable it under the postgresql receiver's metrics; operation=replay, read on the primary, one series per replication_client

cloudwatch.note: RDS read replicas; statistic Maximum, per DBInstanceIdentifier. Aurora's AuroraReplicaLag is in milliseconds, not this

metrics.name: replication.slot.retained.bytes
metrics.label: WAL held for a replication slot (bytes, worst slot)
metrics.description: WAL the server keeps for its most-lagging replication slot. A slow or stopped slot consumer, such as CDC or a replica, lets it grow under write load until the disk fills.
metrics.dimension: per database server, its most-lagging slot

datadog.note: one series per slot: export the max by host

cloudwatch.note: RDS and Aurora PostgreSQL; statistic Maximum, per DBInstanceIdentifier

metrics.name: temp.bytes.rate
metrics.label: Temp files written (bytes/s)
metrics.description: Bytes written to temporary files by queries that ran out of work_mem. Sorts and hashes spilling to disk.

telegraf.note: one series per db tag: export the sum per server

datadog.note: one series per db tag: export the sum by host

otel.note: off by default: enable it under the postgresql receiver's metrics; export the sum per server

metrics.name: temp.files
metrics.label: Temp files created per minute (peak)
metrics.description: Temporary files queries created in any minute of the run, each a sort or hash that ran out of work_mem. It counts the spills where temp bytes measures their size: many small spills hide in a bytes rate.

telegraf.note: one series per db tag: export the sum per server

datadog.note: one series per db tag: export the sum by host

otel.note: off by default: enable it under the postgresql receiver's metrics; export the sum per server

metrics.name: checkpoints.requested
metrics.label: Requested checkpoints per minute (peak)
metrics.description: Checkpoints requested rather than run on schedule, under load mostly because WAL reached max_wal_size, in any minute of the run. Under write load they bring bursts of I/O and latency spikes. On PostgreSQL 17 and later the Prometheus query needs postgres_exporter's stat_checkpointer collector, which is off by default.

telegraf.note: PostgreSQL 16 and earlier: 17 moved it to pg_stat_checkpointer, which the input does not read

datadog.note: a count per check interval; read from pg_stat_checkpointer on PostgreSQL 17

otel.note: type=requested; read from pg_stat_checkpointer on PostgreSQL 17

metrics.name: database.size.growth
metrics.label: Database size growth (bytes/min)
metrics.description: How fast the databases grow during the run, as a slope.

datadog.note: one series per db tag: export the sum by host

otel.note: one series per database: export the sum per server
